Welcome to Kew Green Prep School
Where Childhood and Ambition Grow Together
Welcome to Kew Green Prep School

Welcome to Kew Green Prep School
Where Childhood and Ambition Grow Together
Welcome to Kew Green Prep School
Where Childhood and Ambition Grow Together
The Complete Preparatory Experience
An exceptional 2–11 education in the heart of Kew.
We are a vibrant and nurturing community, where learning is purposeful, joyful, and ambitious. Our school combines academic excellence with a commitment to developing the whole child – intellectually, emotionally, socially, creatively and physically.
Excellent 2026 11+ Results
Kew Green Prep pupils have achieved outstanding 11+ results in 2026, securing places at leading London senior schools.
We are incredibly proud of every pupil – these exceptional outcomes reflect academic ambition, expert teaching and the confidence they carry into the next stage of their education.
An Outstanding Start
Rated Outstanding in all areas by Ofsted, our dedicated team ensures that all children make outstanding progress in their learning and development.
Kew Green Prep Pupils Win Public Speaking Competition
Three Year 5 pupils from Kew Green Prep won the Epsom College Public Speaking Competition against nine other prep schools. Their confident and humorous speech impressed the judges and secured the trophy, reflecting both their excellent communication skills and the strong academic support provided by KGPS teachers.
Our Mission
At Kew Green Preparatory School we see every child as an individual, inspiring and equipping them to be ambitious and achieve success; happy, motivated and able to shape a brighter future for themselves and society more widely.
Why choose Kew Green Prep School?
We achieve outstanding 11+ results, with pupils regularly awarded scholarships to leading senior schools.
Our ambitious approach develops intellectual curiosity, independence and high aspiration, enabling every child to fulfil their potential. Alongside academic excellence, we nurture individual talents and instil strong values of citizenship, responsibility and service, shaping confident young people ready to make a positive contribution to society.
Pastoral and Wellbeing
Co-Curricular
Facilities

Join us at one of our open events for a full tour of our school.
Values
Curiosity
Confidence
Collaboration
Curiosity
Curiosity
At Kew Green, we indulge curiosity, believing that education shouldn’t steer pupils to predict what we want them to predict. Instead, we encourage our pupils to ask bigger and better questions, gaining depth to their understanding and ability to critique, adapt and think abstractly.
Creativity
Creativity
Alongside our strength in our specialist creative subjects and extra-curricular clubs such as Art, Design & Technology and Music, we champion the creative mindset at Kew Green. Our pupils have the confidence to follow their questioning, take educational risks, unafraid to think beyond any ‘box ticking’ formula.
Confidence
Confidence
We believe that self-esteem is fundamental to all aspects of education. The nurturing and development of self-esteem in all our pupils must run alongside our rigorous academic curriculum. We encourage our pupils to have a ‘mindset of a champion’. A Kew Green pupil is articulate, able to communicate clearly. They have a choice, opinions, independence of thoughts and they can pro-actively engage in opportunities and new experiences, showing perseverance and resilience at every step.
Collaboration
Collaboration
We see it as a moral commitment to promote and foster positive and healthy relationships. We have a strong, close-knit community with our ‘open door’ policy for parents further strengthening our partnership. We are one team and parents can be certain that every member of staff knows every pupil and part of their successful journey with us.
Curriculum
A Curriculum that Challenges, Enriches and Prepares
At Kew Green Prep, our ambitious curriculum inspires curiosity, builds strong foundations and prepares pupils to thrive. Through specialist teaching and creative learning, every child is challenged to achieve their best.
Creative Expression and Confident Performance
Drama at Kew Green Prep brings learning to life through role play, performances and expressive workshops that build confidence, communication and creativity. Pupils enjoy class assemblies and main school productions such as nativity plays and Shakespeare adaptations, with extra opportunities in LAMDA and after-school drama clubs to develop their dramatic skills throughout the year.
Creativity at the Heart of School Life
At Kew Green Prep, Art is a vibrant and valued part of everyday learning. Taught by specialist teachers, our exciting and ever-evolving curriculum gives every child the opportunity to excel creatively, drawing inspiration from a wide range of traditional and contemporary artists and creative practitioners. Through ambitious projects and hands-on exploration, pupils develop confidence, skill and a lifelong love of the visual arts.
Enabling students to fully engage in a wide range of sporting activities
All pupils enjoy a broad sports programme that builds fitness, confidence and a love of physical activity. Upper School pupils benefit from top class facilities at Trailfinders Sports Club for fixtures and tournaments and we use Kew Green across all year groups, alongside excellent local facilities for swimming, athletics, hockey and tennis.
News & Updates
Read more articles on all aspects of a Kew Green education as well as expert opinion from our teaching staff.
Considering a Prep School place for September?
If you’re moving to London or exploring Prep School options for Reception to Year 6, our Admissions Team is here to help throughout the summer holidays. Please email Admissions using the button below, and we’ll respond within 24 hours during the working week (Monday–Friday).

Welcome and About Us
At Kew Green Nursery, we pride ourselves on providing a happy, nurturing and secure environment where children feel valued, enjoy learning and can flourish.
Our enthusiastic and dedicated teachers offer children a broad and balanced curriculum. In addition to gaining language, mathematical, scientific and technological skills, they are encouraged to develop enquiring minds, to question, reason and make decisions. During these early years, we hope to promote excellent social skills and we encourage all children to become responsible, confident and independent learners.
Kew Green Nursery is a beautifully spacious environment situated opposite Kew Green, and moments away from Kew Green Prep School. The children that attend Kew Green Nursery have the opportunity to transition to the Reception class at Kew Green Preparatory School, should this be your desired choice.
At Kew Green Nursery we offer the perfect combination of indoor and outdoor learning. The mix of ages in the spacious early years environment encourages a variety of learning opportunities. By providing a balance of adult-led and child-initiated activities, we are able to meet the needs of each child, allowing them to develop at their own pace.
Children can attend Kew Green Nursery the term following their 2nd birthday and join our Hedgehogs Group (2 to 3 years of age).
We recommend our younger children attend for a minimum of three mornings per week. When we feel your child is ready, they will then have the option to stay for more mornings and possibly a few full day sessions.
Our pre-Reception aged children form our Squirrels Group (3 to 4 years of age). We suggest that all our Squirrels attend five mornings and a minimum of three full days to get them used to the longer day before they begin their next journey to ‘Big School’!

About Us
We are a co-educational London Preparatory School and Nursery for children aged 2 – 11. Based in Richmond, we are located on Kew Green. Our school site backs onto the River Thames and is next door to the world-famous Royal Botanical Gardens.
We pride ourselves in finding every child’s skill through the breadth of our curriculum. We offer children the opportunity to succeed, be recognised and be valued. Due to our size, we can say confidently that every teacher in our school knows every single child and that lends itself hugely to that feeling of warmth and closeness. Happy children who have high self-esteem and who feel safe are going to be successful, progress and thrive.
As a London prep school, we prepare our children for the 11+ and are academically ambitious for them, but we also are a true prep school where parents drop off their children and know that almost all their learning and co-curricular activities take place onsite.
As part of the Gardener Schools Group, there is a natural transition to either Kew House School or Maida Vale School; however, we are proud that our children receive offers from a range of top independent schools.

Welcome
Welcome to Kew Green Preparatory School, where childhood and ambition grow together.
We are a vibrant and nurturing community, where learning is purposeful, joyful, and ambitious. Our school combines academic excellence with a commitment to developing the whole child – intellectually, emotionally, socially, creatively and physically. As a staff team and as Head, we always try to make Kew Green the type of place where we wanted to go to school: warm relationships, high expectations without pressure and plenty of fun! Love of learning is the key to everything we do at Kew Green Prep.
We are situated in one of London’s most iconic and inspiring locations, a stone’s throw from the Royal Botanic Gardens, adjacent to the cricket pitch on Kew Green and backing on to the River Thames, offering the benefits of both a city education and a strong connection to nature.
We have a broad and balanced curriculum which seeks to light the flame of curiosity and creativity in every child whilst also unearthing and cultivating their unique talents. Our mission is for Kew Green children to be confident and articulate but also equipped with the skills and knowledge to make a positive impact in the world. We are incredibly proud of our exceptional outcomes and the manner in which we achieve them, through a ‘greenhouse’ rather than a ‘hothouse’ approach.
We ensure that every child flourishes through outstanding teaching, rich and varied opportunities, and strong pastoral care. Our staff know each child as an individual and celebrate their unique strengths and potential. Visitors often comment on the warm and happy atmosphere that pervades our school – it is a place where children feel safe, valued and excited to learn. We build strong relationships with each family through our open door policy, encouraging partnership and a shared vision between home and school.
Whether discovering the wonders of nature along the towpath, taking part in a Shakespeare workshop, composing music, solving maths challenges or forming lifelong friendships, children at Kew Green are supported and stretched in equal measure.
We believe that an outstanding prep education is not just the warm-up act, it is the main event! It is during these years that the brain is most malleable, curiosity is at its peak, and identity begins to take shape, forming the architecture of the brain for years to come. It gives us great joy to help lay the foundations of an exciting journey for your child.
I warmly invite you to visit us at one of our open mornings, or by separate appointment, to experience for yourself the energy, care and excellence that define our school.

Drama
Whether it is through role play in English, hot seating in history, debating in PSHEE, or performing on stage, drama helps children to develop self-confidence, creativity, communication, collaboration, and empathy.
Every class puts on a class assembly each year, to which parents and other visitors are warmly invited. Our main school productions are the Reception Nativity, Year 2 Nativity and the Year 4 and Year 6 productions. Our most recent Year 6 production was a captivating performance of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ adapted by our Head of English, Kate Bennett and Amy Kinross with musical pieces written by our Head of Music, Emily King intermixed with modern pop songs from the likes of Taylor Swift. Previous performances have included several bespoke productions written especially for the children at Kew Green, as well as Peter Pan, Mary Poppins, Oliver, and My Fair Lady.
A variety of workshops are on offer throughout the year, including during our Theme Weeks and Book Weeks, where children can develop their dramatic skills.
Extra-curricular drama is also on offer in the form of LAMDA lessons, which take place during the school day, and after-school drama clubs.

Inspection Reports
Our latest ISI inspection summary offers an independent snapshot of life at Kew Green Preparatory School and Kew Green Nursery.
Rather than focusing on a single measure of success, the report highlights the experiences that shape daily school life. From ambitious learning and specialist teaching to wellbeing, inclusion and strong partnerships with families. We are proud that the inspection recognised not only academic achievement but also the confidence, kindness and sense of belonging that our children develop throughout their time with us.
You can explore our inspection summary below, alongside the full ISI inspection reports, to read the inspectors’ findings in their own words.
KGPS ISI Summary2026
ISI Routine Inspection Report 2026

Kew Green Nursery Ofsted Inspection 2025
Kew Green Nursery Ofsted Inspection 2025
Ofsted visited our Nursery on 12 February 2025 and ran a full statutory inspection and Kew Green Nursery achieved the highest possible grade of Outstanding across all areas as follows:
The inspection teams’ findings were extremely positive and a few of the comments can be found below:
All children make exceptional progress in their learning.
Staff demonstrate an exceptional understanding of how to support children’s thinking skills.
Parents and carers praise the excellent relationships between staff and children.
Children learn a wealth of knowledge through meticulously planned activities that capture a wide range of skills.
Children flourish in a happy and stimulating environment.
– Ofsted Report 2025
The full report can be viewed here, Oftsed Inspection Report February 2025
The quality of education – Outstanding
Behaviour and attitudes – Outstanding
Personal development – Outstanding
Leadership and management – Outstanding
Kew Green Prep ISI Report 2023, 2018 and 2015
We were pleased to welcome a team of Independent Schools Inspectors (ISI) into school in February 2023, who ran a full statutory inspection.
KGPS achieved the highest ISI grade possible:
The inspection team’s findings were extremely positive and we are delighted to have received these comments:
Pupils approach their studies with highly positive attitudes and an evident desire to succeed.
Pupils are self-confident and self-disciplined; demonstrating resilience and perseverance to improve their learning.
Pupils demonstrate a mature moral awareness and take responsibility for their own behaviour.
Pupils are respectful of each other in keeping with the school’s ethos of kindness and care.
The full report can be viewed here, ISI Report 2023

Art
The Art department endeavours to provide an exciting and stimulating environment where pupils feel inspired, eager to learn and empowered to create.
Lessons in Art provide every child at Kew Green Prep with the opportunity to excel creatively through an exciting, diverse, and ever-changing curriculum, taking inspiration from a wide selection of traditional and contemporary artists and creative practitioners.
In our brand-new purpose-built Art and DT Studio, children can explore a broad range of creative activities, with every project and lesson aiming to embody Kew Green’s core values: Curiosity, Creativity, Collaboration and Confidence.
In their weekly Art lessons, pupils are set projects and taught a wide breadth of skills, encouraging curiosity and exploration of ideas, allowing them to gain confidence as independent learners and thinkers. Through guidance and practice, children are encouraged and empowered to continue to develop and refine their skills and the quality of their work, enabling them to produce outcomes they can been truly proud of and celebrate, helping to build resilience and self-esteem.
Art is a truly valued subject at KGPS which is celebrated and championed throughout the school, with the aim that our pupils develop a lifelong appreciation for the visual and creative arts and acquire valuable skills they can apply in their everyday lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education - Kew Green Preparatory School | Sports
pageCache.text:
Physical Education
At Kew Green, we offer a broad and varied curriculum that enables students to fully engage in a wide range of sporting activities. Our goal is to help pupils develop a love for playing sports, become fit and healthy children, and embrace good sporting values. Our Upper School pupils benefit from the use of Trailfinders Sports Club and play regular fixtures and host tournaments at these top class facilities. We also use beautiful Kew Green, right on our doorstep, across all year groups alongside a selection of best in class local facilities for sports such as swimming, athletics, hockey and tennis.
Nursery & Early Years
Lower School (Year 1-2)
Upper School (Years 3-6)
Nursery & Early Years
In Nursery and Early Years, our sports programme is designed to be fun and engaging. Lessons focus on agility, balance, coordination, and teamwork. We gently introduce the rules and equipment for specific sports and activities in a way that is accessible and enjoyable for young children. These high-energy sessions ensure that every pupil learns the importance of progress, focus, and dedication. Activities are structured to promote physical development while also instilling the joy of movement and play.
Lower School (Year 1-2)
As pupils progress to the Lower School, the emphasis on agility, coordination, balance, and fitness continues. We introduce team sports such as football, netball, rugby, and cricket. Basic skills and techniques for each sport are taught through challenges and games, helping children develop transferable skills needed for various sports. Swimming lessons commence in Year 2, providing an essential life skill and an additional avenue for physical development. We also introduce gymnastics, which focuses on flexibility, strength, and body control. These activities aim to build confidence and competence in a supportive and encouraging environment.
Upper School (Years 3-6)
In the Upper School, pupils delve deeper into team sports, with a focus on competitive play. We arrange competitive fixtures every term and host several intra-school tournaments throughout the year. Our pupils also participate in numerous local and regional events, such as the IAPS competitions. This exposure to a higher level of competition helps pupils hone their skills, understand sportsmanship, and experience the excitement of representing their school.
Competitions and Events
Our pupils have the opportunity to participate in a variety of prestigious competitions as well as our own intra-school events, including:
Philosophy and Approach
The sporting programme at Kew Green is designed to improve confidence and skill and ensure that all pupils, regardless of their initial ability, are catered for. We believe in striving for excellence in competitive sports while maintaining a core philosophy that supports all skill levels. pageCache.pageTitle: Crêpes, French And Fun - Kew Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Crêpes, French and Fun
Year 5 at Kew House School
Year 5 pupils from Kew Green Prep enjoyed an inspiring visit to their senior sister school, Kew House, where they took part in a unique, hands-on learning experience using the school’s specialist facilities.
Older Year 9 pupils studying French and/or Food Preparation and Nutrition at Kew House worked alongside the younger children, guiding them through a practical cooking session in the senior school’s fully equipped food technology kitchens. What made the experience particularly special was its cross-curricular focus: all instructions were given in French, requiring pupils to listen carefully, follow directions and apply their language skills in a real-life context.
During the session, pupils made crêpes from scratch, measuring ingredients, mixing batter and cooking their creations while practising key French vocabulary linked to food, utensils and cooking processes. This immersive approach brought Modern Foreign Languages to life, helping pupils see how language learning can be applied beyond the classroom while developing valuable practical cooking skills at the same time.
The session also encouraged teamwork and confidence, as Kew House pupils acted as mentors, demonstrating techniques and supporting their younger peers. Working in small groups, the children collaborated, communicated and problem-solved together, building independence and resilience in a stimulating and supportive environment.
As part of the Gardener Schools Group, Kew Green Prep benefits from close links with its two senior schools, giving pupils access to specialist facilities and learning experiences that go far beyond those typically available in standalone prep schools. These opportunities enhance pupils’ education and provide valuable preparation for senior school life, helping to build confidence, aspiration and familiarity with advanced resources from an early age.
Experiences like this highlight the strength of the partnership between Kew Green Prep and Kew House. By learning in senior-school environments and working with older pupils, children gain insight into the next stage of their education while enjoying rich, engaging and memorable learning experiences that connect subjects in meaningful, real-world ways.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupils Triumph At Epsom College Public Speaking Competition - Kew Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Kew Green Prep Pupils Triumph at Epsom College Public Speaking Competition
Pupils at Kew Green Preparatory School have demonstrated outstanding academic confidence, communication skills and teamwork, winning the prestigious Epsom College Public Speaking Competition.
In December 2025, every pupil in Year 5 took part in an internal public speaking competition, presenting their speeches to their English groups.
Following an impressive first round, numbers were narrowed to three semi-finalists from each group, who then delivered their speeches in front of the entire year group. Judges Ms Bennett, Mr Reed and Mr Harrington had the challenging task of selecting just three finalists to represent KGPS at the competition.
After a closely contested round, Ela, Harrison and Maddie were chosen.
The trio worked closely with Ms Bennett to refine their speech, and developed their ideas, strengthened their delivery and built their confidence to perform on a larger stage.
The team created a humorous and imaginative speech entitled “Eating Sweets is Virtually the Same as Eating Fruit.” Maddie was Chair and spoke for one minute, followed by Ela as the Main Speaker, who spoke for three-minutes and Harrison concluded with the Vote of Thanks, speaking for one minute.
On 4 March, the KGPS team travelled to Epsom College, where they competed against nine other preparatory schools. Topics ranged from “Why Playtimes Should Be Longer” to “AI in the Classroom.”
Thanks to their clarity, humour, confidence and exceptional teamwork, the Kew Green Prep pupils delivered a truly memorable performance. And the result? KGPS won the competition!
Congratulations to Ela, Maddie and Harrison on a fantastic achievement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Young Entrepreneurs Take The Lead - Kew Green Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Year 6 Enterprise Fair 2026
This summer term, Year 6 pupils at Kew Green Prep are swapping their textbooks for business plans as they take on one of the most exciting and rewarding projects of their final year at the school: the Enterprise Fair 2026. Following the conclusion of 11+ exams, our Year 6 cohort is rolling up its sleeves to launch a series of pupil-run businesses, each one designed, marketed and managed entirely by the children themselves.
Working in groups of four to six, the pupils have been challenged to devise an original product or game, develop it from concept to finished stall and sell it to a school-wide audience of customers spanning Reception through to Year 5, as well as teachers and parents. From the very first lesson, the children have been firmly in the driving seat. Each group has completed a detailed business plan, outlining their idea, equipment needs, costings, marketing strategy and predicted profits, before submitting it to staff for sign-off.
The project blends creativity with real-world rigour. Pupils benefit from a Graphic Design workshop led by our Head of Art and DT, sharpening their advertising posters and stall branding, and a Money Matters workshop delivered by a parent working in finance, introducing the children to the fundamentals of bank accounts, saving, debit and credit cards, and how to stay safe from fraud.
What makes the Enterprise Fair so special at Kew Green Prep is its strong charitable heart. Every group selects a charity close to their interests, researches its work and produces a PowerPoint to share with their year group. After the fair, the children write letters to their chosen charities, explaining exactly how they raised their donations.
On the day, customers purchased tokens, sold at 50p each in the mornings and at pick-up, to spend at the stalls. The pupils had an hour after lunch to set up before opening at 2pm, with the fair running until 4pm. Each group nominated a responsible ‘banker’ to look after their money box and every member was expected to stay for the all-important clear-up.
Beyond the buzz of the day itself, the Enterprise Fair develops invaluable life skills: teamwork, leadership, financial literacy, creative problem-solving, resilience and the satisfaction of giving back. It is a fitting send-off for our Year 6 pupils as they prepare to move on to senior school, and a wonderful celebration of the confident, enterprising young people Kew Green Prep is so proud to nurture.

Uniform
At Kew Green Preparatory School, our school uniform plays an important role in fostering a strong sense of belonging, pride and identity within our community. Wearing the correct uniform helps pupils feel equal, focused and ready to learn, reinforcing our shared values and high expectations. We ask all families to support this by ensuring that children attend school each day in the correct uniform, worn smartly and with care.
Our official uniform supplier is Billings & Edmonds, whose dedicated Kew Green Prep uniform shop is located at 112 Chiswick High Road, W4 1PU. All required uniform and sports kit items should be purchased through Billings & Edmonds to ensure consistency, quality and correct branding.
To register as a new customer and purchase your child’s uniform and sports kit, please use the link below:

We also recognise that children grow quickly, and to support families we hold second-hand uniform sales throughout the year. These provide an opportunity to purchase good-quality, pre-loved uniform items at a reduced cost. Parents will be notified directly by the school when a sale is scheduled.

Sample Lunch Menu
At the heart of a Kew Green Prep education is a love of learning, supported by a healthy body and mind. So healthy meals are important. Ensuring growing children get the right nutritional balance we have onsite kitchen which prepares and cooks all our meals from scratch.
Our dedicated in-house catering team provide freshly prepared healthy meals which are varied, nutritious, well balanced and above all, delicious. School menus rotate on a weekly basis and combine seasonal, fresh ingredients to produce healthy lunches.
Sharon Andrews has been the Gardener Schools Group Catering Manager since it was founded. She has qualifications in Nutrition and manages the catering for all school events ranging from parent/staff BBQ events to Canapé Receptions.
All of our schools have a 5-star Food Standard’s Agency Rating which is the highest possible level.
Drinking water is always available at break and lunch times, and additionally throughout the day with chilled water fountains at various points around the school.
Local Suppliers
We are proud that the majority of our food is sourced locally, including meat, fish, vegetables and dairy products which come from independent, local traders.
Dietary Requirements
Every endeavour is made to ensure that individuals with special dietary requirements are met, just as they would be at home. Wherever possible we try not to change the menus for pupils with special dietary requirements but simply adapt the weekly menu to meet their needs.
Allergies
We are a nut free school. We have a number of children with a range of food allergies and this is one of the main reasons we do not allow pupils to bring in a packed lunch or any snacks from home. Our catering staff are alerted to food allergies at the start of every academic year and advise pupils as to the contents of the meals being provided.

Wrap-Around Care
We are aware of the difficulties of working parents who need Wrap Around Care for their child. Our Morning and After School Care is in place to help parents who need to bring their children to school early and who cannot collect them at the end of the afternoon lessons.
Our dedicated, qualified supervision staff ensure the children have the best possible experience and enjoy the various activities and games on offer.
Morning care is available from 8am and afternoon care runs up until 6pm.
Wrap around care can be used on an ad hoc basis whenever it is needed or, parents can register and pre-pay for the full day service at the start of term.
At the end of lessons, (click here for timings of the school day) pupils are given time to eat their snack and a range of interesting games and recreational activities are available to them under the supervision of specially appointed staff. Older pupils may do their homework at this time in a quiet room set aside for the purpose.
There are also a range of afterschool clubs, the majority of which finish at 4.30pm.
£6.00 per child per day. Children can be dropped off at 8am. Children left in supervised care anytime between 8am and 8.30am will be charged.
£6.00 For aftercare until 4:30pm. £5.50 Post club until 5:00pm £14.00 Until 6pm (snack included)
Children can either complete homework or take part in supervised play or activity. Children who stay beyond 5pm will be given a hot or cold snack.

Facilities
Kew Green Preparatory School is often described as ‘a hidden gem’ as it is housed in an attractive four storey building, surrounded by mature trees and nestled in a peaceful corner of Kew Green. Next to the school is The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, which we use regularly and if you take a stroll behind the school’s playground, there is a charming towpath by the River Thames which many of our children use to walk to school.
At the front of the school is Kew Green, a beautiful green space which provides the setting for the majority of PE and Games lessons, including the use of St Anne’s Church which hosts many of our concerts. Our onsite facilities include bespoke classrooms for subjects such as art, design and technology, music, IT and science. We have purpose-built music pods for one-to-one music lessons. Gardener Schools Group
Gardener Schools Group is a family company founded by teachers. It provides an education based on clear values and with the overarching belief that talent must be nurtured so that every pupil reaches their full potential.
The group is comprised of four co-educational schools based in London – Ravenscourt Park Preparatory School, Kew Green Preparatory School and Nursery, Kew House School and Maida Vale School. GSG schools currently educate 1,450 pupils aged 2-18 years. Since 1991, these schools have pursued excellence and innovation while establishing strong family communities at each location.
Our approach is holistic with a balanced focus on a child’s intellectual, moral, spiritual, physical and emotional development. We engender confidence and self-esteem, leading to intellectual risk taking and a love of learning. We cultivate values of respect, compassion, tolerance and community responsibility in each student.
While we retain the traditions we have established over time, we take a fresh approach to all areas of school life and are not bound by current conventions and practice. We encourage individuality of thought and self-motivation in all areas of study and exploration.
We also believe that parents have a great role to play in our schools and we adhere to a genuine “open door policy” meaning that our schools become hubs for their community of parents, students and staff.
Our schools recognise talent, allow pupils to feel they can take risks and bring parents into the process at every stage. This approach leads to excellent academic results, rounded, thoughtful students and happy and energised school communities.
